2: name: rigorous-proof
3: description: Use Yui to make an existing proof self-contained as concise mathematical NL0 with independent Audit A, then optionally translate it through reviewed frozen interfaces into Lean with machine Audit B. Supports NL0-only, accepted-NL0 translation and full workflows; structural checks and compilation alone do not establish source fidelity.
4: ---
5: 
6: # Yui: mathematical NL0 and Lean implementation
7: 
8: Use the smallest requested track. Preserve the original problem, hypotheses,
9: definitions and proof route. The two stages share one specification and explicit
10: invalidation rules; completing stage one does not require stage two.
11: 
12: The installed skill root is the directory containing this `SKILL.md`. Keep
13: `config.json`, `nl0/`, `nl02lean/` and `toolchain/` beside it; no enclosing
14: `rigorous-proof/` subdirectory or particular checkout name is required.
15: 
16: ## Select a stage
17: 
18: Before dispatch, follow [target selection](nl0/references/target-selection.md).
19: Resolve a clear intended theorem yourself without asking again; ask the user
20: only when the intended target remains ambiguous. Freeze the complete selected
21: statement(s), including standing assumptions, as an explicit job input.
22: 
23: The invoking agent owns request/configuration collection and dispatch. Follow
24: [installed operation](nl0/references/operation.md) to identify explicit proof inputs,
25: ask once for missing active-phase model/reasoning/speed settings and, for a
26: NL0, full or translation request, an explicit per-case worker count N, then call
27: `nl0/scripts/yui.py run` (or prepare/execute). Retain settings already supplied by
28: the user; do not call a separate intent-classification model. Do not silently
29: choose a worker count from defaults or `auto`; obtain a positive integer or
30: the user's explicit confirmation of a proposed number. N bounds local R-node
31: reviews and, in a separate phase, local Lean proofs. NL0/Audit A and
32: Lean preparation/proofs/assembly/Audit B have separate phase profiles. The user
33: does not prepare queues, task packets or controller jobs manually.
34: The invoking owner follows [foreground handoff and monitoring](nl0/references/owner-observation.md):
35: normally dispatch with `--detach`, verify the owned processes, and register one
36: host heartbeat for a bounded check every ten minutes. Record the actual schedule
37: ID, report that mathematical work is still pending, then end the current
38: foreground turn. Never keep the owner active through sleep/poll loops. Each
39: scheduled check ends its turn as well. `DISPATCHED` is not workflow completion.
40: If host scheduling is unavailable, disclose that and return manual status/cancel
41: commands; do not claim that a monitor was registered. Frozen author/proof/reviewer
42: stages perform only their assigned roles and never schedule owner monitoring or
43: redispatch the workflow.
44: 
45: For missing external originals, follow [ordered source retrieval](nl0/references/source-retrieval.md):
46: arXiv, Google full-text search, Google DOI discovery, then confirmed-DOI Sci-Hub
47: lookup with ordinary browser readback when needed. Reuse an already available
48: adequate primary source; retrieval alone does not establish theorem fidelity.
49: At invocation disclose the [conditional-source policy](nl0/references/conditional-sources.md):
50: inaccessible primary texts can permit continued work from complete explicit
51: secondary statements, but the final result remains conditional. Show each
52: actual warning and include warn.json/warn.md in the final report. Never label
53: unverified sources or a qualified workflow as an ordinary full PASS.
54: 
55: Default permanent output is `<problem-directory>/rigorous-proof/<run-id>/`,
56: outside the installed skill. Multiple problems own separate outputs, contexts,
57: queues and ledgers. Use normal local repair unless a first-pass measurement is
58: explicitly requested. Runtime and software controls are fully inside this skill;
59: no repository example/support directory or old test result is required.
60: New jobs retain an allowlisted executable/rule/catalog snapshot in their owned
61: `runtime/` directory and launch from it. Installation updates cannot silently
62: change an active job's bound code; snapshot tampering still fails validation.
63: Historical jobs without snapshots retain their original binding checks.
64: Each native Lean call defaults to a five-minute wall limit. Yui proof workers
65: automatically receive frozen ST020 repair advice after a verified native
66: wall/heartbeat limit, through the same failed tool result. Keep the target and
67: inputs unchanged, repair in the same worker, and recheck. General strategy-bank
68: queries remain optional; this failure-triggered advice needs no extra model call.
69: Follow [fault treatment and authorized exit](nl0/references/error-lifecycle.md).
70: Local Python retries recognized temporary service/network faults every 60seconds,
71: at most 30 times in the same carrier/thread. Other faults and exhausted retries
72: enter a retained `PAUSED_ERROR`, notify the owner through local `codex queue`,
73: and wait for an exact-incident operator action. An error never authorizes task
74: termination or workspace deletion. Release only the completed roles at the
75: specified global-pass, all-local-pass, interface-freeze and final-delivery
76: boundaries, after their bound handoffs are saved. Explicit user cancellation or
77: a selected B-final user decision is a separate authority. Keep
78: scientific evidence and the selected profile. A pause is nonterminal: never
79: restart it or delete its monitor. Existing exited-run recovery is historical,
80: not a substitute for live `resume-error` controls.
81: An explicitly authorized `--after-access-restored` continuation separately
82: supports a verified provider HTTP403 stop at the NL0/Audit A boundary. It checks
83: authenticated model metadata without inference before preparation and launch;
84: 403 stays excluded from automatic retries. Preserve old faults/costs and disclose
85: the new runtime and unreleased-author scope in that operation reference.
86: For a previously stopped inherited probe-directory collision, the same operation
87: reference documents a separate guarded `--repair-local-tool` continuation after
88: verified software repair and explicit owner authorization; it restores the saved
89: located author repair rather than restarting the original proof.
90: The separate guarded `--repair-native-cleanup` route supports an actually exited
91: frozen proof queue stopped only by verified native-process cleanup faults. It
92: preserves the exact source/A/interface, rechecks completed local bodies and
93: restores only the failed worker's own bound drafts; never use it to resample a
94: mathematical nonpass or replace live work.
95: 
96: Normal translation requires a separate independent semantic interface review
97: before freezing and proof dispatch. Normal final Audit B is machine-only: verify
98: that actual E/P, their defining environment and complete proof dependencies still
99: match that reviewed authority. Only a valid-proof/interface-drift exception opens
100: an actual independent B-final model review, with warning-qualified delivery.
101: Follow [proof diagnosis and reviewed repair](nl02lean/references/proof-repair.md).
102: Local compiler defects return to their own author; explicit global proof-connection
103: issues go to the serial connection author. It cannot change frozen E/P or their
104: meaning-determining definitions. No fixed idle-turn threshold retires a round or
105: cancels sibling jobs. Frozen-contract/source defects wait for the user.
106: 
107: 1. **NL0 and Audit A.** Use [Audit A's shared acceptance requirements](nl0/references/audit-a.md#shared-mathematical-acceptance-requirements)
108:    as the single mathematical standard for both author and auditor. Prefer concise grouped
109:    review and batch completion; ordinary background facts require mathematical
110:    conditions and justification, not a pre-translation native probe.
111:    Read [the NL0 stage](nl0/references/nl0-stage.md),
112:    [format](nl0/references/nl0-format.md), [self-containment](nl0/references/self-containment.md),
113:    [authoring](nl0/references/nl0-authoring.md), and Audit A's role-specific execution protocol.
114:    Read [external-source review](nl0/references/external-theorems.md) for citations
115:    and [logical packaging](nl0/references/logical-rules.md) for local assumptions.
116:    Use `nl0/scripts/nl0.py`; its explicit accounting is not a mathematical prover.
117:    Controllers and reviewers follow [completion and local repair](nl0/references/review-execution.md)
118:    for global-first parallel R coverage, exact evidence inheritance and stage boundaries.
119: 2. **Translate an accepted NL0 and run Audit B.** Verify the supplied Audit A
120:    authority and exact source version first. This workflow requires audit-format-4
121:    authority; do not relabel a detailed-NL0 format-3 receipt. Do not reconstruct or re-audit an
122:    unchanged proof. Start with [minimal translation](nl02lean/references/minimal-translation.md).
123:    Read [translation](nl02lean/references/stage.md),
124:    [the working sequence](nl02lean/references/integrated-workflow.md), and
125:    [Audit B](nl02lean/references/audit-b.md). Operators use
126:    [execution and file-based control](nl02lean/references/execution-protocol.md)
127:    for parallel queues, status and stops; workers need only their frozen packet.
128:    After local proofs complete, the controller first attempts mechanical
129:    [assembly and source-facing export](nl02lean/references/assembly.md).
130:    Use the serial connection author only for actual connection/library-discharge
131:    repair. Normal final machine Audit B inherits the frozen semantic review;
132:    B-final is reserved for proof-valid interface deviation.
133:    Use
134:    `nl02lean/scripts/source_preparation.py` for bounded shared extraction,
135:    then `workflow.py` for source/IR freeze, proof work and final gates.
136: 3. **Full workflow.** Complete track one, then track two. A changed mathematical
137:    statement or new theorem returns to the affected NL0/Audit A boundary.

139: ## Mathematical invariants
140: 
141: - Accepted NL0 is a complete natural-language proof relative to explicit H/E/M,
142:   fixed logic and its hash-bound mathematically reviewed background supplement. Important
143:   tools remain explicit; ordinary correct elementary reasoning needs no
144:   exhaustive calculation chain. See [background notes](nl0/references/background-notes.md).
145: - Within NL0, each inference uses only its direct inputs, global definitions and explicitly
146:   established in-scope local facts or mathematically checked node-local background
147:   notes. Exact routine Mathlib declarations are resolved during translation.
148:   Notes never add H or repair a substantive gap. Source papers and producer proof bodies do
149:   not fill gaps in a task packet.
150: - Preserve one global mathematical identity while allowing local Lean views.
151:   Actual cross-view conversions need checked proofs. In stage two, the pinned
152:   Mathlib environment is freely available without NL0 M registration.
153: - Shared mathematical extraction is a bounded local change at translation entry.
154:   Review its new producer and substitution cuts; inherit unchanged evidence.
155:   Freeze the revised NL0 before final IR and worker packets.
156: - Local conditional bodies may run concurrently. Assembly must discharge every
157:   internal dependency with an actual checked proof; conditional checks alone
158:   are not a final result.
159: - The independent pre-freeze review checks every E and complete P, including
160:   hypotheses, quantifiers and relevant definitions. Final machine Audit B checks
161:   actual exported full types and complete closure against that frozen authority.
162:   Supply short direct/equivalent correspondence explanations. Check actual Lean
163:   closure and trust, without a Mathlib-to-NL0 use ledger.
164:   Neither author notes nor a compiler pass are semantic approval.
165: - Stop on a judged substantive mathematical gap. Ordinary expansion and local
166:   verifiable corrections remain allowed. Difficulty or elapsed time does not
167:   establish that a mathematical claim is false.
168: 
169: ## Clean execution and accounting
170: 
171: Operators use [execution terminology](nl0/references/terminology.md) to distinguish
172: Codex conversations, native subagents, Yui jobs, worker slots and controllers.
173: Use the logical phase names **NL0 worker**, **preprocessing worker**,
174: **formalization workers (N slots)** and **postprocessing worker**. A logical
175: worker may contain several separate author/reviewer threads and program steps;
176: N limits concurrent local R reviews and local Lean proof jobs in their separate phases.
177: Report executor termination separately from mathematical acceptance.
178: 
179: Read [isolation](nl0/references/isolation.md) and [measurement](nl0/references/measurement.md)
180: before any model test or benchmark. Run model authoring, planning, proof and
181: review stages through the isolated carrier. The interactive developer's memory,
182: other personal skills, expert packages, old task outputs and hidden reference
183: proofs are never an input source for these stages.
184: 
185: The Yui arm receives only the declared Yui rules and task material. The direct
186: arm receives a minimal task/tool contract and the same mathematical inputs,
187: without Yui planning, strategy or shared-proof guidance. Log controller-supplied instructions, frozen inputs, native configuration,
188: tool schemas/results, reported model identity, phase, usage and health. Native
189: Codex manages model networking and context; Yui does not intercept HTTP payloads.
190: Actual tier and per-response usage coverage remain unknown when not exposed. Never execute model-generated Python or shell text.
191: 
192: Collect the active phase profiles as described above. `config.json` supplies
193: defaults only when explicitly selected. The current isolated native Codex carrier requests
194: Standard speed and checks model/effort availability without fallback. Freeze
195: and record each stage's selected profile;
196: never silently substitute a stronger model or fallback.
197: Resolve the confirmed concurrency before dispatch and record its basis; do not
198: claim an unknown backend maximum. N limits local R-node reviews, then local
199: Lean proof jobs in a later phase. NL0 authoring, global Audit A, preparation,
200: interface work, assembly and Audit B use one serial lane per case.

## Original exercise

Elias M. Stein and Rami Shakarchi, *Real Analysis: Measure Theory,
Integration, and Hilbert Spaces*, Princeton Lectures in Analysis III,
Chapter 7, Problems, exercise 9, printed page 388.
Book DOI: [10.1515/9781400835560](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400835560).

> 9. Let \(E\) be a compact set in \(\mathbb R^{d-1}\). Show that
> \(\dim(E\times I)=\dim(E)+1\), where \(I\) is the unit interval in
> \(\mathbb R\).

## Fixed interpretation and complete target

Here dimension means **Hausdorff dimension**. As approved by the user on
2026-10-23, assume explicitly that \(E\) is nonempty. With the convention
\(\dim_H\varnothing=0\), the printed equality would otherwise fail for
the empty set. This is a disclosed addition to the printed exercise.

compact set, and put \(I=[0,1]\). Identify \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R\)

3: Audit A's shared section is the mathematical authority. The policy is
4: mathematical-background-v2-1. Ordinary mathematics is reviewed in NL0; exact
5: Mathlib implementation is resolved in nl02lean.
6: 
7: ## Eligibility and record
8: 
9: A note records a correct, routine local step with actual available premises,
10: no new hypothesis, no missing project lemma and no new core proof route.
11: Give id (BG001 etc.), kind (elementary or mathematical), at (an existing
12: /inference/argument/N/text pointer), fact (precise mathematical statement),
13: grounds ([{location,reason}] for real available conditions), and justification
14: (actual mathematical reasoning). A familiar name alone is insufficient.
15: Non-native notes have no source field or claim of a verified Lean declaration.
16: The optional record_background_note tool saves a checkpoint; a complete review
17: may submit all its notes in one artifact without separate tool calls.
18: 
19: For example, continuity of a sum follows from the supplied continuity of the
20: functions and continuous addition on their actual codomain. Check those
21: conditions mathematically. The reviewer need not call Lean or identify
22: Continuous.add before judging that routine step.
23: 
24: Substantive missing arguments, changed quantifiers, missing witness existence,
25: unsupported limit exchanges and uncertain external statements remain blocking.
26: The controller validates structure and local pointers; it never decides that
27: a mathematical fact is true or routine. An actual independent reviewer owns
28: that decision and may return FAIL or UNVERIFIED.
29: 
30: ## Handoff
31: 
32: The immutable author graph and hash-bound review notes jointly describe the
33: accepted mathematical proof. The format-4 receipt is not a format-3 verified native
34: background policy. Explicit native mathlib notes can still be inspected only
35: with their complete matching pinned evidence; they are optional, not a new
36: requirement for routine mathematical notes.
37:

39: paragraphs and do not become additional premise ports. Workers find appropriate
40: library declarations or prove auxiliary facts with their actual conditions.
41: The interface author chooses shared representations, not every local tactic
42: or implementation lemma in advance. Every required fact must eventually be
43: established in checked Lean. No note is an axiom or a new external E.
44: 
45: The source supplement hash and exact notes are bound in the interface contract,
46: worker packets and Audit B source inventory. They cannot be dropped, borrowed

1: # Accepted NL0 revision, frozen translation and Audit B
2: 
3: This is the execution guide for Yui's translation stage. Preserve the accepted
4: original NL0/Audit A. The runtime adapters compose their existing checks;
5: Python handles exact edits, versions, scheduling and evidence. Models/humans
6: still inspect mathematics, choose Lean representations and author local plans.
7: Automatic semantic compilation of arbitrary papers is not claimed.
8: 
9: ## 1. Inspect before extracting
10: 
11: ```sh
12: python3 scripts/source_preparation.py inventory \
13:   --graph /absolute/original/nl0.json --spec /absolute/original/spec.json \
14:   --audit-a /absolute/original/audit-a.json
15: ```
16: 
17: The result contains canonical direct consumers and exact paragraph hashes/text.
18: Start from existing exports. Inspect repeated derivations and their scopes;
19: do not ask a model to reprove or rewrite every node. Zero useful candidates is
20: valid: keep the accepted original and skip revision entirely. Fanout is not
21: avoided proof cost. Tiny helpers may cost more to discover/review than they save.
22: 
23: Models may propose candidates; select only existing derivations with a clear
24: closed interface. No automatic optimal selection or exhaustive discovery is
25: promised. Keep discovery, selection and owner intervention visible in costs.
26: 
27: ## 2. Stage a bounded patch
28: 
29: `patch.json` has `version: "nl0-local-revision-1"`, `baseline_graph_sha256`,
30: `spec_sha256`, optional `discovery_and_author_cost_seconds` and `candidates`.
31: Each candidate has exactly:
32: 
33: - `id`, `proposition`: one complete new internal N record;
34: - `producer`: one complete new R record under the parent current-v2 schema;
35: - `derivation`: `{inference: R_ID, paragraphs: [S_ID, ...]}` pointing to the
36:   already supplied derivation;
37: - Put the baseline revision/old R/S and current producer separately in the new
38:   proposition's origin. Historical provenance is not a current dependency edge.
39: - `expected_avoided_work`: a concrete basis, with unmeasured assumptions disclosed;
40: - `consumers`: at least two distinct actual consumer records.
41: 
42: Each consumer has `inference`, `before_sha256` (the canonical sorted JSON hash
43: of the old R), `inputs`, `replacements`, optional retained `applications`, and
44: `cut`. The direct inputs may retain/remove old ones and add only this new N.
45: Each replacement gives the stable `paragraph`, `before_sha256` of its full old
46: paragraph, and preferably `splices: [{old, new}, ...]` plus `uses_after`.
47: Every old string must match once, with no overlapping spans. Unselected text
48: is preserved byte for byte. Optional `uses_local_after`/`objects_after` adjust
49: the explicit accounting. A complete `after` paragraph is also supported for
50: small paragraphs, but cannot change local fact records or assumption lifetimes.
51: 
52: `cut` gives `old_conclusion`, `shared_instantiation`, `supplied_conclusion`,
53: `conditions: [{condition, justification}, ...]`, and `continuation`. Spell out
54: bindings, domains, exceptional sets/representatives and every fact/object the
55: untouched continuation needs. A new citation alone is not substitution.
56: 
57: Do not change original H/E/M/D, logic, target, old proposition statements, or
58: unrelated arguments. The adapter rejects overlapping consumer patches, added
59: consumer source applications and changed local-fact/assumption lifetimes.
60: Defer unsupported edits instead of expanding to a full proof rewrite.
61: 
62: ```sh
63: python3 scripts/source_preparation.py stage \
64:   --graph /absolute/original/nl0.json --spec /absolute/original/spec.json \
65:   --audit-a /absolute/original/audit-a.json \
66:   --patch /absolute/patch.json --out /absolute/new-revision
67: ```
68: 
69: The output contains unchanged-spec `case/spec.json`, revised `case/nl0.json`,
70: exact source dependencies, producer/cut packets, pending review templates,
71: patch and binding manifest. Never overwrite an accepted stage. A later revision
72: may supply `--incremental /absolute/previous/source-acceptance.json` instead of
73: ordinary `--audit-a`; the adapter revalidates its chain and rejects cycles.
74: 
75: ## 3. Complete actual scoped reviews and accept the revised source
76: 
77: Fill `case/producer-review.json` only from actual fresh reviews of each complete
78: producer packet. It uses ordinary parent Audit A entries, including checks,
79: located evidence, source applications and exact fresh-packet replay boundaries.
80: The producer-only reviewer need not establish the old derivation's provenance
81: or whole-graph acceptance from a packet that lacks those materials.
82: 
83: Fill `case/cut-review.json` from the paired cut packets. Its checks are
84: `existing_derivation`, `condition_discharge`, `conclusion_match`,
85: `continuation_preservation`, `dependency_accounting`. Require an actual verdict,
86: specific notes, evidence and the paired `/before`, `/after`, `/contract`,
87: `/old_derivation`, `/producer_source_derivation`, `/shared_statement`, `/input_statements_before`,
88: `/input_statements_after`, `/global_context` locations. Evidence paths are relative
89: to `case/`, as in the parent checker. This is delta review with baseline access,
90: not a new independent fresh replay of the whole consumer. E/M applications
91: retain the parent schema; N uses belong in inputs/citations/explicit prose.
92: `old_derivation` is this consumer's actual replaced baseline proof.
93: `producer_source_derivation` is the one selected original proof of the shared
94: intermediate result, which may come from another consumer. Different final
95: consumer goals are expected; compare the shared intermediate conclusion instead.
96: Keep each generated `packet_sha256`: a review from a different cut packet cannot
97: be reused merely because IDs and pointer names coincide. Exact reuse after
98: record-only changes requires byte-identical source and actual reviewed packets,
99: with original verdicts, evidence, carrier and acquisition cost retained.
100: 
101: ```sh
102: python3 scripts/source_preparation.py check --out /absolute/new-revision
103: ```
104: 
105: This writes `source-acceptance.json`. It retains original audit qualifications,
106: records new-full/substitution/inherited coverage and invokes the parent rules
107: for new producers. Unchanged consumers/downstream conditional arguments need
108: no new mathematical replay when their inputs, context and conventions remain
109: unchanged. Python still rechecks the graph and exact preserved bytes.
110: 
111: `INCREMENTAL-AUDIT-A-PASSED` requires an accepted current-v2 baseline and every
112: actual local review. A missing/unverified baseline yields development-only local
113: review and cannot enter the complete production gate. No new receipt falsely
114: claims the parent issued a fresh whole-graph audit-v3 pass. Hashes do not prove
115: mathematical correctness or authenticate a reviewer who fabricates judgment.
116: 
117: ## 4. Author and freeze the IR
118: 
119: Choose object views, input/output types, planned typed conversion interfaces, shared
120: ports and local T plans jointly. Preserve natural NL0 node boundaries. Export
121: every fact needed by another task; no shared result is an ambient definition.
122: The source graph is now fixed. Representation/API difficulties remain Lean
123: engineering; substantive source changes require a separately reviewed revision.
124: 
125: For the whole workflow the contract's relative `source.path` points to exact
126: canonical NL0 bytes, not a summary. `source_steps` copy every argument paragraph
127: with distinct implementation IDs. The controller copies these paragraphs and
128: note locations from the accepted source rather than asking the author to
129: transcribe them. The author supplies types and local plans, and can save partial
130: JSON before completing the whole interface.
131: 
132: The lower-level mechanical freeze uses a checked binding with
133: `source_graph_sha256`, `contract_sha256`, `plan_sha256`, `paragraph_mapping` and
134: `source_outputs`. It checks exact source coverage and direct boundaries and runs
135: Lean type elaboration. This binding is **not a semantic review receipt**; the
136: recorded semantic status is `PENDING_AUDIT_B`. This legacy route requires explicit semantic review before claiming complete
137: acceptance. Normal full/translation entry runs the independent interface reviewer
138: and reads back its actual hash-bound PASS before freezing/dispatch; final machine
139: Audit B inherits it only after actual full endpoint and proof-integrity checks. The commands below expose the
140: lower-level compatibility path; use `--interface-review` to supply an actual
141: review when constructing a workflow manually. See [repair routing](proof-repair.md).
142: 
143: ```sh
144: python3 scripts/workflow.py freeze /absolute/new-workflow \
145:   --graph /absolute/new-revision/case/nl0.json \
146:   --spec /absolute/new-revision/case/spec.json \
147:   --incremental /absolute/new-revision/source-acceptance.json \
148:   --contract /absolute/interface/contract.json --plan /absolute/interface/plan.json \
149:   --interface-binding /absolute/interface/accepted-interface-paths.json \
150:   --max-concurrency auto
151: ```
152:
